analysis:
This batch contains only documentation: a new changelog fragment (changelog.d/gptoss-bf16-activations.md) and a one-line edit to the activation-floor row in docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (line 97). No source code is supplied, so the underlying SwiGLU dtype change, the K/V sizing change and the checkpoint-namespace change are not visible. I reviewed these claims as described, not as implemented.

Security-relevant claims:
1. GPT-OSS SSD checkpoints written with float32 layer types fall into a different checkpoint namespace and are not restored. This is consistent with T-041. Stale ciphertext stays at rest until the 30-minute sliding TTL expires it or a KEK wipe purges it. It remains HMAC-named and AES-GCM protected, so no new at-rest exposure is introduced. The changelog claim that old files expire depends on the selected volume staying mounted. That is a pre-existing caveat already recorded in T-041.
2. Native K/V per token is halved, so slot grants hold about twice as many tokens. The 3.5 GiB activation floor is explicitly noted as measured on the float32 path and not re-measured for bf16. This is a memory-admission and availability question, not a confidentiality one, and the docs openly record the gap. bf16 activations should reduce activation memory, so the float32 floor is conservative. The doubled token capacity per grant is the only possible pressure, and admission reportedly uses the observed native K/V dtype. Whether it does so correctly is unverified here.
3. Output is no longer bit-identical. This affects consumer-visible determinism and does not touch the coordinator or provider trust boundary. T-007 concerns a malicious provider, not this accuracy shift.
4. The heartbeat kv_bytes_per_token halves. The coordinator-side servability and capacity policy is platform-owned and was not supplied, so cross-repo agreement is unverified.

No findings. Follow-up for a code-bearing pass: confirm that the checkpoint identity includes layer dtypes, so bf16 and float32 caches cannot cross-restore. Also confirm that admission uses the observed dtype rather than an assumed one.
